applies_why: Yes: the judge cites the almah/bethulah word-count cutting both ways as a reason for UNDERDETERMINED.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: A verse that carries two senses at once is not open; I weighed whether the word-count-cuts-both-ways phrase treats the verse as open/UNDERDETERMINED (forbidden) or merely notes evidence on both sides (allowed).
why: Using the disputed word evidence as cutting both ways to leave the issue UNDERDETERMINED treats an ambiguous single verse as open, contrary to K-S2's requirement that both senses stand.
